idiom_name: presentation helper functions over snprintf/vsnprintf in a view module
implementation_notes: C has no template engine and no helper framework, so the pattern is realized by hand: the view is an emitter that walks the model and prints markup, and every helper is a pure function that formats one value into a caller-supplied buffer with snprintf (or vsnprintf for variadic wrappers). The classic helper class has no analogue - the helper unit is the function - and the separation that matters is that helpers own no I/O and no state: the emitter owns the FILE* or socket, the helper only produces text. Where a small template library is used instead of hand-written emitting, the same functions become the engine's callbacks.
pitfalls: snprintf returns the length the output would have needed, so a return value greater than or equal to the buffer size means truncation - treating any positive return as success is the classic C bug.
snprintf's result is undefined when the destination overlaps an input argument, so a helper must never be used to append into the same buffer it reads.
A helper that writes to the response stream directly (printf/fwrite) cannot be unit-tested and interleaves badly when the emitter is buffered or multi-threaded.
